# A 100.00 USD invoice, and a 200.00 USD bank transaction sitting loose in the
# book — the shape a bank feed leaves behind, before anything says which
# invoice it pays.
#
# Attaching it with `txn_guid:` + `prepayment: 100` is the retarget path, which
# reaches the overpayment mechanic by a different route than the
# `account:`/`settled_amount:` payment block does: no money is moved, an
# existing transaction is divided in place. The residue is a credit of 100.00
# USD the book holds and owes back, and it has to open a basis like any other
# — priced at what the invoice was carried at, since a USD payment into a USD
# bank states no CAD figure anywhere.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable USD
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

customer "C-US"
	name: "US Customer"
	currency: USD

invoice "INV-USD-RETARGET"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-RETARGET"
		accumulate: true
